body.p:
Aʼsdas was a gambler, then he lost. He did so again, he bet again / his property. Then he did so again, he bet / other property. Then he gambled again, he did not gamble long
before he lost again. / Then he had lost again. He staked his one / child and he began to gamble again. It was the same as before, / he had not gambled long before he had lost his child. Then he gambled again, he staked another / child and he did not gamble long before, he lost his other child. / He did so again, he staked another child. Aʼsdas was gambling with a woman. Then he gambled again and / it was the same, he had not been gambling long before, / he lost his child. / Then he staked his sister. It was the same again, he did not gamble long before he had lost his sister. / Then he did so again, he staked his / other sister. It was the same. He did not / gamble long before he lost / his other sister. Then he staked his wife. Then it was the same again, he did not gamble long before he lost / his wife. Then Aʼsdas staked again. Now really / he staked his house. He did so again, / he began to gamble. Aʼsdas was playing on the ground and Aʼsdas had not been gambling long before / he lost his house. Then / he did so again, he staked himself. He began to gamble again. He / was gambling on the ground and Aʼsdas had not been gambling long before he lost. / Now he was a slave. Then he walked without caring where he went.
He started away. He walked up the river / and he did not know where he was going. He had not been going long / before he reached a house. He entered. / Aʼsdas came unexpectedly. "Come in Aʼsdas, I am tired waiting for you." Then he did so again. / He started again, it was the same way, he had not / been going long when a child was walking about playing in front of the door / where he went. Then Aʼsdas went there and killed it. / He due a hole for the one that he had killed and buried it. Then he left it on the ground. It was not, / long before he arrived at the house, the house of the father / [of the child.] He entered there. Then there was only the wife of / North-East Wind. Aʼsdas threw the wife of North-East wind on her back / and she lay with her back towards the fire. Then he cohabited with her by the side of the fire. After they had cohabited / she asked, / 'Did you not, see my child?" He answered "No". / She said to Aʼsdas "Do not keep a secret I know you. You will get a supernatural treasure from me. / Let us go and get him." Then he went. He arrived at the burial place / and dug him out. Then he sprinkled him with the water of life of his mother. They / went to her house. Then they were going to make fun of Aʼsdas. The wife of the North-East Wind turned over her blanket, and Aʼsdas stuck in one corner of the house, on one side of the house of North-East Wind. / Aʼsdas stuck against the wall of the house. / Then she turned it again and it became summer in the / house of North-East Wind Aʼsdas became free again. Then Aʼsdas was going to have this for his supernatural treasure. / The wife of North-East Wind gave him her blanket. He was
instructed, "If anyone does mischief to you / just turn it over." / He was also given bird down and / water of life. She said, "Take care of that village. There is a bad man. You will lose if you / gamble with him. He will kill you." / Then he went again and he arrived there. / "You are a gambler, come here, / Aʼsdas." He put down a gambling mat. Then they were about to give him food. After we have given you food, / we will gamble." Then Aʼsdas ate. / After they had given him food he / spread out the mat, and then he gambled.' He / put up a stake. They played with gambling sticks. Then they gambled. He almost lost all his sticks. Then they began to play. Then he almost lost sometimes. Then the man with whom Aʼsdas was playing / did almost the same. / Then they finished. Then the one against whom Aʼsdas staked made up his mind. "Do not go away quickly Aʼsdas. Now I / will go up that we may eat meat. You will get firewood ready in the house / that we may cook the meat." Then he went. / "As soon as you see [the game] dropping down / then go and get firewood." Then he shot, he who went up the mountain and it fell down the one he had shot, / that. is a mountain goat fell down. Aʼsdas went, / to get firewood. Aʼsdas chopped once / with his axe and it became full of notches. / "That is bad," said Aʼsdas. He cut across, then the axe was whole gain, then / Aʼsdas cut the firewood into blocks. He carried it on his shoulders. He carried it into the house. / The firewood
was on the ground / outside of the house. Then arrived the mountain climber and cut up [the goat]. He butchered it. After he had finished cutting it up he put stones on the fire. / He took the stones out and the meat was done. / They ate it. Then Aʼsdas was sent / to go up the mountain. He was given arrows. Then / Aʼsdas went. Aʼsdas had not been climbing long when he saw a mountain goat. He came to it / and he had not been standing long on the rock / when the place on which Aʼsdas stood rolled down. / Then the whole mountain rolled down. Aʼsdas put the bird's down on the rock and went into / the down. Then Aʼsdas was on top of the slide. / He rolled down with it. / How he had rolled down with it, but / Aʼsdas did not give up. He went up to the same place. It was not very high. Then he saw another / goat. He reached it and shot it. Then fell down the goat. He reached it and skinned it and / carried it down on his back. He walked along and went home. He reached the house and entered the house of his play-fellow. Now he was going to take revenge, / he was going to do mischief to him. / He wore the blanket of the wife of the North-East Wind. He turned it over. / Then he stuck to the wall of the house. He stuck / in the rear of the house, Then Aʼsdas threw over his wife and she stuck to the floor. He did mischief to him. / Aʼsdas cohabited / with
his wife. After he had finished, / she instructed him. "You will go / a long ways up to the house of Nnōʼaqaua." Then Aʼsdas went. / He had not been walking long when Aʼsdas saw a village. Aʼsdas walked along and arrived there. / Then he did the same as before. He went right up and entered / the house of Nnōʼaqaua. "You came here suddenly, Aʼsdas. You are a gambler / Aʼsdas." Aʼsdas was / addressed just in the same way. / "After you have been given to eat, let us gamble." Then Aʼsdas was given food. / They finished in the house. Aʼsdas was an ugly man. / They finished giving him food. / Then they began to play. Nnōʼaqaua spread out / a mat and Aʼsdas did the same. / He spread out his mat. / Then Aʼsdas and Nnōʼaqaua gambled. Neither he nor Nnōʼaqaua won. / "Let us finish," said Nnōʼaqaua. / Then Nnōʼaqaua made up his mind. "Let your gambling sticks be my gambling sticks. That, is, let us exchange our gambling sticks." Then Aʼsdas gave him his gambling sticks and / Aʼsdas exchanged his gambling sticks for those of Nnōʼaqaua. / Then the body of Aʼsdas was made right. / He was sprinkled with the water of life of / Nnōʼaqaua. Then he was sprinkled with the water of life of / Nnōʼaqaua. He was becoming good looking. Now Aʼsdas was a good looking man. / Now Aʼsdas was a real man. / Aʼsdas was a really good looking man. He was asked "That, is to be your supernatural gift? / Aʼsdas was told by Nnōʼaqaua. Then / Aʼsdas was given his supernatural gift. He was given the beaver, bear, mountain goat, grizzly bear, deer, wolverene, wolf, fox, lynx,
land otter. There was nothing / that was not given to him and he was also given the martin, / mink, racoon, marmot, and porcupine. / All these were given to him as his supernatural gift. Then he was sent away. Then Aʼsdas started / and went along. Aʼsdas was going home. So / Aʼsdas was a good-looking man. Then Aʼsdas was desired / on account of his appearance. Then Aʼsdas went along again. / He went and arrived at his house. Then Aʼsdas arrived at the house of the one who had done mischief to him. Then he turned / the one who had done mischief to him on his back. He threw him over on his back and he also threw over his wife. / Then he cohabited with her. He cohabited / with the wife of the one with whom he had played. After he had / cohabited with her he took off the East-Wind blanket. Then he put it on. It became summer and the ice melted in the house of the / big man. He left them / and went along and came to the house of North-East Wind. / He entered again and again, he threw on her back the wife of North-East Wind. / He cohabited with the wife of North-East Wind. After he had done so Aʼsdas went along. He was about to go home / to his house. It was not long before he reached inland / from his village. Then he sat down at the side of / the place where the tribe used to draw water. He had not been sitting very long / before two women arrived to draw water at the place for drawing water. "A good looking man is sitting there at the side / of our place for drawing water," said the women. / Then the younger sister arrived on the ground. "Who are you?" said / the younger sister. Thus asked him the younger sister. "I am Aʼsdas. / Let us get married," said Aʼsdas to the woman. "Your father will obtain a treasure from me when we are married.” / Then the woman went and arrived at their father's. The
woman told her father, "Aʼsdas said he wants to marry me," / said the woman to her father. "He is not / good enough to marry you. He is a bad, ugly man,” / she was told by her father. "Do you think you would recognize him? / You will obtain a supernatural treasure from him. You will obtain a supernatural treasure from him. Go to him, / If you do not believe, that you will get a supernatural treasure from him.' / Then she went again with her father. They arrived where Aʼsdas was sitting on the rock. / He did not believe that Aʼsdas was changed. Down to the ground reached his hair. Then he went to / the place where he was sitting. Then Aʼsdas spoke and said that / he wished her for his wife. [He said,] "I love her."
